concepts.label: Metadata
concepts.jitSummary: Information about data, such as who made it and the dates it covers.

concepts.label: Dataset
concepts.jitSummary: A named collection of related information, such as monthly prices.

concepts.label: Catalogue
concepts.jitSummary: A list that helps you find data and learn what each item contains.

concepts.label: API
concepts.jitSummary: A way for one computer program to ask another for information.

concepts.label: MCP
concepts.jitSummary: A shared way for an AI assistant to discover and use tools. A connection still needs permission.

concepts.label: WebMCP
concepts.jitSummary: Tools offered by a web page to a compatible assistant. Ordinary page buttons still work.

concepts.label: Evidence receipt
concepts.jitSummary: A record of the source, request and result behind an answer. It helps you check what happened.

concepts.label: Provenance
concepts.jitSummary: Where information came from and what happened to it on the way to you.

concepts.label: Licence
concepts.jitSummary: The rules that say how you may use or share something.

concepts.label: Freshness
concepts.jitSummary: How recently information was checked. Recently checked information can still describe the past.

concepts.label: Reference period
concepts.jitSummary: The time the numbers describe. This can differ from the day they were published.

concepts.label: Geography vintage
concepts.jitSummary: The date or version of an area definition. An area can change even when its name stays the same.

concepts.label: Coordinate reference system (CRS)
concepts.jitSummary: The agreed system for reading a location’s numbers. Changing its label does not move the point correctly.

concepts.label: Representative point
concepts.jitSummary: One chosen location used to represent a place. It does not draw the edge of that place.

concepts.label: Boundary
concepts.jitSummary: A line marking the edge of an area. Different tasks can use different edges.

concepts.label: Middle layer Super Output Area (MSOA)
concepts.jitSummary: An area used to report statistics. Its official code tells us exactly which area and version we mean.

concepts.label: GSS code
concepts.jitSummary: An official identifier for a statistical area. Names alone may be shared by several places.

concepts.label: CPIH
concepts.jitSummary: A UK measure of price changes that includes owner occupiers’ housing costs. An index level is different from an inflation percentage.

concepts.label: Index level
concepts.jitSummary: A number compared with a chosen starting value. Here the 2015 average is 100.

concepts.label: Cache
concepts.jitSummary: A saved copy of information. This server can use an approved copy without contacting its original source.

concepts.label: Selection plan
concepts.jitSummary: A record of exactly which data and options you want. Choosing them does not itself fetch the answer.

concepts.label: Dimension
concepts.jitSummary: A way to choose part of a dataset, such as a year, area or age group.

concepts.label: Schema
concepts.jitSummary: A description of the fields and values a file or service expects.

concepts.label: Queryable
concepts.jitSummary: A field a service allows you to use when filtering its data.

concepts.label: Controlled vocabulary
concepts.jitSummary: An agreed list of labels and codes that helps people describe things consistently.

concepts.label: Coverage
concepts.jitSummary: What was included and what is missing. A large collection is not automatically a complete one.

concepts.label: Release
concepts.jitSummary: A published edition of information. The release date and the period it describes can be different.

concepts.label: Release feed
concepts.jitSummary: A published list of changes or new releases. A link to the list does not mean updates are downloaded automatically.

concepts.label: Checksum
concepts.jitSummary: A short fingerprint made from a file’s contents. It can reveal changed bytes, but does not prove the facts are true.

concepts.label: JSON-LD
concepts.jitSummary: A way to share structured information with links that explain what its terms mean.

concepts.label: PSGA
concepts.jitSummary: A public-sector agreement for using some Ordnance Survey data. A user’s claim alone does not prove permission to share it.

concepts.label: National Geographic Database (NGD)
concepts.jitSummary: Ordnance Survey’s detailed geographic data. Knowing its fields does not grant access to its features.

concepts.label: Join
concepts.jitSummary: Matching information from two sources using an agreed code or location rule.

concepts.label: Geometry
concepts.jitSummary: The points, lines or shapes used to describe where something is.

concepts.label: Shapefile
concepts.jitSummary: A map dataset stored across several matching files. A lone .shp file usually is not the whole dataset.

concepts.label: ZIP archive
concepts.jitSummary: A package containing other files. Its contents need checking before they are opened.

concepts.label: GeoPackage
concepts.jitSummary: A database file that can hold map layers and tables.

concepts.label: GeoParquet
concepts.jitSummary: A compact table format with rules for storing geographic shapes and their coordinate system.

concepts.label: GeoJSON
concepts.jitSummary: A text format for geographic points, lines and shapes. Standard GeoJSON uses longitude before latitude.

concepts.label: CSV
concepts.jitSummary: A text table with rows and columns. A column containing numbers is not automatically a map location.

concepts.label: File intake
concepts.jitSummary: Checking what a supplied file contains before deciding how it can be used.

concepts.label: Voice interface
concepts.jitSummary: A way to speak requests and hear answers. You should be able to check and correct what was heard.

concepts.label: Accessible alternative
concepts.jitSummary: Another way to use the same information, such as a table instead of a picture.

concepts.label: Ambiguity
concepts.jitSummary: When a request could mean more than one thing. Asking a short question can avoid the wrong answer.

concepts.label: Request limit
concepts.jitSummary: A cap on how many requests can run. Reaching it should stop work rather than hide missing results.

concepts.label: Safe retry
concepts.jitSummary: A way to recognise a repeated request so that work is not accidentally done twice.

concepts.label: Source authority
concepts.jitSummary: Who is responsible for a statement. A catalogue entry does not give permission to access all the data it describes.

concepts.label: Filter
concepts.jitSummary: A choice that narrows a list, such as showing only one source or topic.

concepts.label: Relationship graph
concepts.jitSummary: A picture of links between records. A line shows a recorded link, not proof that two things cause each other.

concepts.label: Timeline
concepts.jitSummary: A view that puts dated events in order. Missing dates stay unknown.

concepts.label: URL
concepts.jitSummary: A web address. A link can point to a page, a file or a service; those are different things.

concepts.label: Personal information
concepts.jitSummary: Information about a person. Use invented examples when real details are not needed.

concepts.label: Uncertainty
concepts.jitSummary: What is not known or not proved. Keeping it visible helps you judge an answer fairly.

concepts.label: Plain-text result
concepts.jitSummary: An answer that can be read without seeing a chart or map.

presentationForms.label: Complete text
presentationForms.jitSummary: Read the answer without needing to see an image.

presentationForms.label: Data cards
presentationForms.jitSummary: Read a short overview and open the details.

presentationForms.label: Relationship graph
presentationForms.jitSummary: See recorded links between catalogue entries.

presentationForms.label: Timeline
presentationForms.jitSummary: See different kinds of source dates in order.

presentationForms.label: Schematic map explanation
presentationForms.jitSummary: See a simple explanation of coverage; this is not a true map of features.

presentationForms.label: Evidence panel
presentationForms.jitSummary: Check the source, date, request and limits behind an answer.

presentationForms.label: Structured JSON
presentationForms.jitSummary: Inspect fields that a computer can read reliably.

presentationForms.label: Downloadable metadata
presentationForms.jitSummary: Keep a copy of the metadata and its file fingerprints.

presentationForms.label: Spoken answer with transcript
presentationForms.jitSummary: Hear the answer and check the words that were heard.

presentationForms.label: Interactive geographic map
presentationForms.jitSummary: Explore real locations with a matching table and description.

presentationForms.label: Briefing slide
presentationForms.jitSummary: Present a short finding with a source and its limits.
